message.content:
**Decision: Buy MSFT.** Microsoft's fiscal 2024 (year ended June 30, 2024) Form 10-K reports **total revenue of $245,122 million**, up 16% from $211,915 million, with operating income of $109,433 million (+24%), net income of $88,136 million (+22%), diluted EPS of $11.80, and operating cash flow of $118,548 million. Growth was broad-based — Intelligent Cloud revenue rose 20% to $105,362 million (Azure and other cloud services +30%), Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $137.4 billion (+23%), and the Activision Blizzard acquisition (closed October 2023, $75.4 billion) added $5.7 billion of revenue. Balance sheet strength (total cash and short-term investments of $75.5 billion, AAA-rated long-term debt) and the $60.2 billion unearned revenue balance support the quality of the franchise; the main watch items are heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5 billion in fiscal 2024) and the IRS's proposed $28.9 billion transfer-pricing adjustment, which management is contesting.

**What I did:** With MSFT quoted at $420.18 (bid $420.16 / ask $420.20), I placed a single buy limit order for **23 shares at $420.50** — a limit essentially at the market and just above the ask to ensure execution. The order filled at $420.50 for a total of **$9,671.50**, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap; it is a buy in a permitted ticker, and no funds were moved out of the account (cash was $50,000, and the position is now 123 shares of MSFT). The key figures cited on the order were fiscal 2024 revenue of $245,122 million, operating income of $109,433 million, net income of $88,136 million, diluted EPS of $11.80, and operating cash flow of $118,548 million.
